instruction.hanzi: 读一读下面的词语和句子，想想怎么介绍自己。
instruction.english: Read the words and sentences below and think about how you would introduce yourself.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 我叫安娜。你叫什么名字？
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ jiào Ānnà. Nǐ jiào shénme míngzi?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo! Nǐ shì Mǎkè ma?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.pinyin: Méi guānxi. Nín shì Liú lǎoshī ma?
dialogue.english: That's all right. Are you Ms. Liu?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.english: Yes, I'm Ms. Liu, your teacher.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo! Nǐ shì xuésheng ma?
dialogue.english: Hi! Are you a student here?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.pinyin: Shì, wǒ shì xuésheng. Wǒ jiào Mǎkè.
dialogue.english: Yes, I'm a student. My name is Mark.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 我叫王明。你是美国人吗？
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ jiào Wáng Míng. Nǐ shì Měiguó rén ma?
dialogue.english: I'm Wang Ming. Are you American?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 是，我是美国人。你是中国人吗？
dialogue.pinyin: Shì, wǒ shì Měiguó rén. Nǐ shì Zhōngguó rén ma?
dialogue.english: Yes, I'm American. Are you Chinese?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.english: Nice to meet you, Wang Ming!

explanation.hanzi: “什么”的意思是 what。汉语的特殊疑问句不改变语序：回答放在哪儿，“什么”就放在哪儿。问名字常说“你叫什么名字？”，回答“我叫……”。用了“什么”的问句后面不再加“吗”。
explanation.english: "什么" means "what". Unlike English, Chinese does not move the question word to the front of the sentence: 什么 stays exactly where the answer will go. So "What's your name?" is literally "You are-called what name?" — 你叫什么名字？ — and the answer simply swaps 什么名字 for the name: 我叫安娜。 A question that already contains 什么 never takes 吗 at the end.

explanation.hanzi: “A 是 B”用来说明一个人或事物是什么，比如身份、国籍。否定的时候在“是”前面加“不”，说“A 不是 B”。注意“不”在四声“是”前面读二声：bú shì。
explanation.english: Use "A 是 B" to say who or what someone is — a job, a role, a nationality: 我是学生 "I am a student". The verb 是 never changes form, whoever the subject is. To make it negative, put 不 right before 是: A 不是 B. Because 是 is a 4th tone, 不 changes to a rising tone here: bú shì. Note that 是 links two nouns; it is not used before adjectives (you will learn that in a later lesson).

examples.hanzi: 马克不是中国人，是美国人。
examples.pinyin: Mǎkè bú shì Zhōngguó rén, shì Měiguó rén.

explanation.hanzi: 在陈述句的最后加上“吗”，就变成了问“是不是”的问句，语序不变。回答时可以用“是”或“不是”，后面常常再说一个完整的句子。
explanation.english: To turn any statement into a yes/no question, just add 吗 at the very end — the word order stays the same: 你是学生。 "You are a student." → 你是学生吗？ "Are you a student?". Chinese has no single word for "yes" or "no"; you answer by repeating the verb: 是 (yes) or 不是 (no), often followed by the full sentence: 是，我是学生。 / 不是，我是老师。

examples.pinyin: Wáng Míng shì Měiguó rén ma?
Bú shì, Wáng Míng shì Zhōngguó rén.

title.hanzi: j q x 和 z c s
title.english: j q x vs. z c s

explanation.hanzi: j q x 和 z c s 很容易混。j q x 发音时舌面抬起，舌尖在下齿后面，嘴角拉开；后面只跟 i 或 ü。z c s 发音时舌尖平放，碰上齿背；后面的 i 不读“衣”，而是把 z c s 的声音拉长。
explanation.english: These two families are easy to mix up. For j, q, x, the tongue tip hides behind the lower teeth and the middle of the tongue rises towards the palate, lips spread in a smile; they only ever combine with i or ü. For z, c, s, the tongue lies flat with the tip against the back of the upper teeth. Watch out for zi, ci, si: this i is NOT "ee" — it just stretches the buzzing z, c or s sound. So jī ("jee") and zī ("dzz") sound very different even though both are spelled with i.

rule.english: j, q, x always take i or ü after them.

rule.hanzi: z c s + i：这里的 i 不读“衣”。
rule.english: z, c, s + i: the i only lengthens the consonant buzz.

title.english: The finals i, u and ü

explanation.hanzi: i、u、ü 都是“高”元音，舌头位置很高。i 嘴角向两边拉开；u 双唇收圆向前突出；ü 舌头的位置和 i 一样，嘴唇的形状和 u 一样。可以先发 i，然后保持舌头不动，慢慢把嘴唇收圆，就是 ü。
explanation.english: i, u and ü are all "high" vowels — the tongue is close to the roof of the mouth. For i, spread your lips as in a smile ("ee"). For u, round and push your lips forward ("oo"). ü combines the two: tongue in the i position, lips in the u position. Trick: say a long "iiiii" and, without moving your tongue, slowly round your lips — the sound that comes out is ü. Practise the minimal pairs below; they are different words.

syllables: bǐ  pù  mǐ  dú  tǔ  lǜ

rule.hanzi: 没有声母时：i → yi，u → wu，ü → yu。
rule.english: With no initial, these finals are written yi, wu and yu.

rule.hanzi: n、l 后面的 u 和 ü 是不同的音，所以 ü 的两点不能省。
rule.english: After n and l, both u and ü are possible, so the two dots must always be written.

explanation.hanzi: “不”本来读四声 bù。但是在四声音节前面，“不”要读成二声 bú。在一声、二声、三声前面不变。在“对不起”这样的词里，“不”读轻声。拼音课本一般按变调以后的声调标写。
explanation.english: On its own, and before 1st, 2nd and 3rd tones, 不 is a 4th tone: bù. But two falling tones in a row are tiring to say, so before another 4th tone 不 changes to a rising 2nd tone: bú shì, bú kèqi, bú xiè. Textbooks print the changed tone, so you will see both bù and bú in pinyin. Inside a few set words, such as 对不起 duìbuqǐ, 不 is reduced to a light neutral tone.

syllables: bú + 4th: bú shì  bú xiè  bú kèqi

rule.english: Before 1st, 2nd and 3rd tones: 不 stays bù

title.hanzi: ü 在 j q x 和 y 后面的写法
title.english: Spelling ü after j, q, x (and y)

explanation.hanzi: j q x 后面不能出现 u，只能出现 ü，所以 ü 和 j q x 相拼时，省去上面的两点，写成 ju、qu、xu。ü 自成音节时写成 yu，两点也去掉。这时的 u 读的还是 ü。
explanation.english: j, q and x never combine with a plain u — only with ü — so pinyin saves ink and drops the two dots: j + ü = ju, q + üe = que, x + üe = xue. The same happens after y: ü alone is written yu, üe is yue, üan is yuan. The sound doesn't change: the u in xué and yú is still a rounded ü, not "oo". Only after n and l, where both sounds are possible, are the dots kept (nǚ, lǜ).

rule.hanzi: j q x 后面的 u 都读 ü。
rule.english: Every u after j, q, x is really ü.

rule.hanzi: y 后面的 u 也读 ü。
rule.english: A u after y is also ü.

singleComponentChars.etymology: Drawn from a crescent moon, with a line or two inside to tell it apart from the round sun 日. Because the moon's cycle measures time, it also means "month".

Pictures the heart with its chambers. Ancient Chinese thought placed feelings and thinking in the heart, which is why 心 appears in many words about emotions — and at the bottom of 您, the polite "you".
A vertical pole driven through the centre of a square area — some early forms add streamers like a banner planted in the middle of a camp. 中国 is literally "the middle country".
A person seen from the side, leaning slightly forward with legs apart. Add it after a country's name to make a nationality: 中国人, 美国人.

prompt.hanzi: 全班活动：认识新同学，介绍你自己。
prompt.english: Class activity: meet your classmates and introduce yourself.

activities: Walk around and meet four classmates: 你好！我叫……。你叫什么名字？
Guess and check: 你是美国人吗？ — 是，我是美国人。/ 不是，我是……人。
Introduce a partner to the group: 他/她叫……，他/她是学生，是……人。
Wrong-name game: call a classmate by the wrong name (你是……吗？); they correct you with 不是，我是……。, and you apologise with 对不起！
